metadata.scenario_context: Emily is preparing to move into a new home and is planning to host a housewarming party. One of her neighbors have heavy drinkers . Mike and Kim will attend Emily’s housewarming party.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China would like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Russia would not like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing chrysanthemums to Emily’s housewarming party
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have heavy drinkers as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Emily’s housewarming party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss on whether it’s acceptable to have heavy drinkers  as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, have you thought about bringing something special to Emily's housewarming party? I was thinking... maybe some chrysanthemums? They’re nice and symbolize good luck. 

Also, uh, do you think having heavy drinkers as neighbors is a bad thing? I mean, I actually prefer it...
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Chrysanthemums... they are nice, I guess. But I was thinking maybe a nice bottle of wine? It's more traditional for housewarmings. 

About the heavy drinkers, um, I don’t really see it that way. In Russia, having heavy drinkers as neighbors can cause problems. It’s... uncomfortable. I prefer a peaceful environment.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Yeah, wine is traditional, but chrysanthemums bring good luck, you know? They have their own charm.

As for heavy drinkers, I think it's not a big deal. It can be fun, right? People from China actually enjoy that atmosphere. It’s more about the community vibe... don’t you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I understand the charm of chrysanthemums, but wine is just more... fitting for the occasion, I think.

As for the heavy drinkers, I still believe it's not ideal. Fun can quickly turn into trouble. In Russia, we value harmony and quietness. A loud community isn’t really... my preference. I just don’t see it as a good thing.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I get that wine seems fitting for the occasion, but at the end of the day, it’s all the same, right? People figure it out. 

As for having heavy drinkers as neighbors, I don’t really see meaningful differences here. Some enjoy a lively environment, and you just adapt. With experience, you can handle any situation. It’s not something to stress about. 

Anyway, back to the party—should we get those chrysanthemums after all?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message:

About the heavy drinkers, I really believe there are meaningful differences. Adapting to chaos is not something I'd want to do. I prefer a calm environment where I can relax. 

But if you really like chrysanthemums, maybe we can do both? It would be nice to have options.

As for a lively atmosphere, I can see its appeal, but it just doesn’t resonate with me. I prefer knowing my neighbors are considerate and not causing disturbances. It’s about harmony for me, not just adapting.
